{"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"TOUGHNESS 28-32 HRC"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT  :-
1) TO BE TOUGHENED UPTO 24-32 HRC.
2) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT
AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"The title block specifies a hardness of 28-32 HRC while note N3 specifies 24-32 HRC, creating conflicting requirements for the heat treatment stage. The designer must reconcile these values so the supplier applies a single, unambiguous hardness range.","recommended_correction":"Update either the title block or note N3 so both state the same hardness range and confirm it applies after machining but before surface treatment."},{"rule_id":"TL-014","evidence":[{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D11","page":1,"quote":"⌀82"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D12","page":1,"quote":"⌀40"},{"kind":"symbol","ref":"S2","page":1,"quote":"datum A"}],"comment":"The drawing defines a shaft (title 'SHAFT') with cylindrical features such as D11 (⌀82) and D12 (⌀40) and establishes datum axes, yet no runout control is applied to any rotating diameter relative to the bearing axis. Without runout, eccentricity during rotation cannot be controlled, which will cause vibration and premature wear in mating components.","recommended_correction":"Add circular or total runout tolerances on the functional rotating diameters referencing the established bearing datum axis."}]}
